passage: Yusuf here, at the desk across from Kalyani in the logistics office. Thursday was the day forty trucks got rerouted because of the flooded highway. By noon I noticed her cheeks drawn in tight, like she was biting the insides of them, and every few minutes she blew out a long breath that puffed her whole face out. I couldn't tell if she was angry at the drivers, at our manager, or just worn out. Then she pushed back her chair, said "Five minutes," and walked to the window by the water cooler. She stood there rolling her shoulders and looking at the rain. When she came back, her jaw looked looser. I slid a printout of the pending routes onto her desk and asked, "Want me to take the southern ones?" She nodded. "Yes. Thank you."

When I got this teaching job she just nodded, said "Achha," and quietly made my favourite kheer that night. So when Mr. Kulkarni, our principal, looked at the corner with an almost still face and said only "Good use of space," I didn't panic. I waited. The next week he asked me to show the other teachers how I'd built it.

But afterwards I knocked on Mr. Rao's door and said quietly, "Sir, I'm worried about the two-week promise. The looms need three." He frowned, then changed the date. Sunaina Apa,
You told me to write when it was done, so here it is. Last night I told Ammi and Abbu I'm leaving the bank job to train as a chef.
I had the speech ready. But when I got to "I've been unhappy for two years," my lips started trembling like a kid's and my voice cracked. Abbu looked alarmed. I think he thought I was ill or in some trouble.
I remembered what you did before your own big talk: stop, breathe slowly, let the silence sit. So I did. Three slow breaths. Ammi just waited, her hand on the table near mine.
Then I finished properly. They didn't say yes. Abbu said, "Let us think." But they listened to all of it, and that's more than I'd hoped for.
Your nervous cousin,
Rafiq

He was quiet a long time. Then: "My eyes. The markings are small. I can't see them any more." It wasn't defiance at all. We got him a better lamp. But mind you, if a jaw comes with a raised hand or shouting, you don't stay to ask questions. You walk out and call someone.
